title: Indian Navy Rescues All 20 Crew From Hijacked Iranian Vessel After 48-Hour Operation
excerpt: The Iranian fishing vessel Azini, seized by Somali pirates on October 29, was located and intercepted more than 3,000 km from Mumbai, with Indian Air Force support.
body:
• The Indian Navy has rescued all 20 crew members of the Iranian fishing vessel Azini, hijacked by Somali pirates, in a 48-hour operation, officials said.
  • The operation was carried out more than 3,000 km from Mumbai in the Arabian Sea, with timely support from the Indian Air Force, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said.
  • Azini was seized on October 29 between the coastal towns of Bandar Bayla and Hafun in northeastern Somalia.
  • Reports do not state what happened to the pirates; the crew and the vessel were both released safely.

The Indian Navy has rescued all 20 crew members of a fishing vessel hijacked by heavily armed Somali pirates in the Arabian Sea, completing a coordinated 48-hour operation more than 3,000 km from Mumbai, according to Hindustan Times. The Navy located and intercepted the vessel and secured the release of the crew and the ship on Monday, with support from the Indian Air Force.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh congratulated the Navy on X for successfully locating, intercepting and securing the release of the Iranian fishing vessel Azini and its crew. The operation was carried out on November 2 through a coordinated effort, he said.

"The swift localisation, interception and safe release of the crew and vessel from significantly armed pirates, with timely support from the Indian Air Force, speak well of the Indian Navy's high operational readiness."

— Rajnath Singh, Defence Minister, on X (as reported by Hindustan Times)

Singh said the personnel had again demonstrated India's ability, intent and resolve to safeguard lives, uphold maritime security and ensure stability across the Indian Ocean Region, and congratulated the Navy for what he called a meticulously coordinated operation.

How the hijacking unfolded

Azini was seized by Somali pirates on October 29. It was hijacked between the coastal towns of Bandar Bayla and Hafun in northeastern Somalia, Hindustan Times reported, citing Associated Press reporting. Fears had been raised that the vessel could be used as a base for further attacks on commercial shipping, amid a resurgence of Somali piracy across the Gulf of Aden and the western Indian Ocean, where several hijackings have been reported in recent weeks.

The reports do not state the number of pirates involved, and do not say whether any were detained; they record only the localisation, interception and the safe release of the crew and vessel.

The standing patrol behind the rescue

The rescue sits inside a much longer deployment. At any given time, one Indian warship has carried out round-the-clock anti-piracy patrols in the Gulf of Aden since October 23, 2008, Hindustan Times noted — a presence intended to protect Indian sea-borne trade, instil confidence in seafarers and deter pirates. A 48-hour rescue completed 3,000 km from Mumbai is the distance that standing deployment is designed to cover.
